qa_pairs.question: Which multimeter setting should I use to test the air temperature switch terminals?
qa_pairs.answer: Use voltmeter setting M01 to test between terminal 4 and terminal 10.

qa_pairs.question: What voltage reading indicates a faulty air temperature switch at cold temperatures?
qa_pairs.answer: If the voltmeter displays at least 9 volts with an air temperature of < -8°C (< 18°F), the switch is faulty.

qa_pairs.question: Do all E30 models have an air temperature switch?
qa_pairs.answer: No, cars with manual transmission do not have an air temperature switch.

qa_pairs.question: How are the wire plugs connected on the air temperature switch?
qa_pairs.answer: Wire plugs for air temperature switch are connected with each other.

qa_pairs.question: What ohmmeter reading indicates a good air temperature sensor at cold temperatures?
qa_pairs.answer: The ohmmeter should display approximately 0 ohm with an air temperature of < -8°C (< 18°F).

qa_pairs.question: What should I do if the ohmmeter shows 0 ohms on both plug connections of the air temperature sensor?
What voltage reading indicates the air temperature sensor is okay at warm temperatures?
qa_pairs.answer: The voltmeter should display approximately 0 volt with an air temperature of > +4°C (39°F).

qa_pairs.question: What resistance reading should I expect from a good air temperature sensor at warm temperatures?
qa_pairs.answer: The ohmmeter should display at least 100 k-ohms with an air temperature of > +4°C (39°F).

qa_pairs.question: How do I test the air temperature sensor resistance?
qa_pairs.answer: Connect ohmmeter (M06) on both plug connections of air temperature sensor after pulling off both wire plugs.

qa_pairs.question: When can I conclude that the air temperature sensor is okay?
qa_pairs.answer: Air temperature sensor is okay when it shows approximately 0 volt at warm temperatures (> +4°C/39°F) during the voltage test.
